purpose: Test whether race-lap derived acceleration, sustained-speed and back-5F push features add stable out-of-sample predictive value beyond the current remaining-600m/relative-closing model.

source_theory.principle: Do not treat raw 200m seconds as horse ability. First convert race-level lap demands into condition-relative features, then estimate what each horse has previously demonstrated under those demands.

race_level_features.acceleration: Within the final 4F, maximum positive acceleration = previous split seconds - next split seconds. Residualize against the starting split level and race conditions so a trivial 13.0->12.0 move is not treated the same as 11.8->10.8.
race_level_features.peak_speed: Fastest final-4F split, converted to a time-aware condition-relative z score.
race_level_features.sustain: Low dispersion / low fade across the final 4F, while controlling for the mean level of those splits. A uniformly slow 4F is not high sustain.
race_level_features.back5_push: For races where non-overlapping front/back 5F are meaningful, front5F - back5F; positive means the race accelerated strongly into the latter half. Use a separate shorter-distance analogue rather than overlapping 5F windows.
race_level_features.depletion: Late fade shape after the fastest point, condition-relative. Used only as a supporting feature, not a standalone negative score.

horse_level_pre_race_features.window: previous 5 starts only; strictly before the target race
capacity_features: best demonstrated acceleration demand in a non-poor prior performance
best demonstrated sustained-speed demand in a non-poor prior performance
best demonstrated back-5F push demand in a non-poor prior performance
horse_level_pre_race_features.leakage_rule: All condition standardization and imputation for a target date must be fit using earlier races only. Current-race realized laps are never inputs.

inference.comparison: paired delta versus A0 on the identical race cohort

adoption_rule.required: Directionally positive in 2024, reproduced in 2025, and still positive in 2026 on the primary ranking metrics without a material finish-gap degradation.
adoption_rule.not_enough: A visually appealing theory, an in-sample gain, or one favorable subgroup is not sufficient.
adoption_rule.production: Only accepted features may alter FinishScore. Rejected/uncertain features may be shown as beta/context labels only.
